Ankang Municipal Communications Bureau.desc: The transport bureau of the Ankang municipal government in southern Shaanxi, China. It administers and maintains the local and provincial roads in the municipality and monitors their condition, while county road administration bureaus and townships look after county, township and village roads.

sources.title: China - Shaanxi Ankang Road Development Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P075613)

Changji Railway Company.desc: A Chinese railway project company, formed in April 2011, that owns and runs the Changchun-Jilin line (111 km) and the Jilin-Hunchun line (360 km), together named the Changchun-Hunchun railway. The Shenyang regional railway administration is a major shareholder; the company's 2016 revenue was about RMB 1.2 billion.

sources.title: China - JiTuHun Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P122321)

Chengdu Railway Bureau.desc: One of the 18 regional railway bureaus of China's state railway system - administrations, attached to the former Ministry of Railways and from 2013 to China Railway Corporation, that operate and maintain the network in their area; the Chengdu bureau's area includes Guizhou province. All 18 were re-registered as companies wholly owned by China Railway Corporation in November 2017, this one as China Railway Chengdu Group Co., Ltd.

sources.title: China - Third National Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P086515)
Railway reform picks up steam (18 local bureaus of the former Ministry of Railways converted into companies)
18个铁路局完成公司制改革工商变更登记 (all 18 railway bureaux renamed China Railway ... Group Co., Ltd., wholly owned by China Railway Corporation)

China Railway Corporation.desc: China's national railway operator: a wholly state-owned enterprise set up in 2013 to take over the operating and construction business of the Ministry of Railways, which was abolished. It has no shareholders' meeting; the Ministry of Finance performs that role for the State Council. Registered capital was RMB 1.74 trillion and it managed a 124,000 km network in 2017. It was restructured and renamed China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. on 18 June 2019.

sources.title: China Railway Corp becomes China State Railway Group Co
China State Railway Group inaugurated
Rail Operator Launches Streamlining, Promises No Layoffs

Cuijiaying Complex Management Office.desc: A special-purpose unit created by the Hubei Provincial Transport Department, and staffed with its people, to build the Cuijiaying navigation and hydropower complex on the Han River and then to manage and operate it once built. The Bank's completion report describes no existence or business beyond that complex.

sources.title: China - Fifth Inland Waterways Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P085333)

Electricity of Vietnam (EVN).desc: Vietnam's state-owned electricity utility, organised as a holding company and active in all parts of the electricity business. Five subsidiary power corporations handle distribution and retail supply at 220 kV and below in their franchise areas. The World Bank's own records and its project documents give the name in English as Vietnam Electricity (EVN).

sources.title: Vietnam - Distribution Efficiency Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P125996)
Vietnam - Second Rural Energy Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P074688)
Projects API record for P074688, Second Rural Energy Project (implementing agencies field)

Guangdong Provincial Waterway Bureau.desc: The waterway agency of Guangdong province in southern China, working under the Guangdong Provincial Transport Department (formerly the Guangdong Provincial Communications Department). It builds provincial waterway works and assigns operating units to run them; local waterway bureaus do routine maintenance and dredging on budgets allocated by the provincial government.

sources.title: China - Fourth Inland Waterways Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P077137)

Guangdong World Bank Financed Projects M.desc: A Guangdong provincial office, placed inside the provincial Department of Finance, that handles World Bank-financed projects in the province. In its comments on the Bank's completion report it stated that it regards itself as the supervising agency for such projects rather than the implementing agency.

sources.title: China - Guangdong Pearl River Delta Urban Environment Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P075728)

Guangxi Xijiang Waterway Construction an.desc: A Guangxi company that builds, operates and maintains navigation-and-power complexes on the Xi River system in southern China. By the time the Naji complex was finished it was already running similar complexes at Guigang and Guiping, and it went on to build another at Yuliang and a second ship lock at Guigang. The Bank's report does not state who owns it.

sources.title: China - Fourth Inland Waterways Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P077137)

Guangzhou Sewerage Treatment Company (GS.desc: Guangzhou's municipal wastewater company, set up shortly before 2004 as a financially autonomous enterprise to run the city's sewage treatment; its service area then covered 6 of Guangzhou's 12 districts. At the start it could not collect tariff revenue itself: the Guangzhou Municipal Finance Bureau collected the fees and reallocated them to municipal departments including the company.

sources.title: China - Guangdong Pearl River Delta Urban Environment Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P075728)

GuiGuang Railway Company Limited.desc: A single-purpose Chinese railway company, incorporated on 4 June 2009 as Guiyang-Guangzhou Railway Company Limited, which succeeded the GuiGuang Railway Company Preparation Group (formed 28 November 2007) to build and then run the Guiyang-Guangzhou line. The line opened in December 2014 as a 250 km/h passenger railway.

sources.title: China - Guiyang Guangzhou Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P107559)

Guiyang Municipal Government.desc: The city government of Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou province in south-west China. At the time of this project the municipality covered 8,034 square kilometres and took in two urban core districts, four peri-urban districts, a county-level city and three mainly rural counties; Guizhou then ranked lowest of China's provinces for GDP per head.

sources.title: China - Guiyang Transport Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P093963)

Huai River Basin Commission.desc: A river basin management agency of China's Ministry of Water Resources - one of seven such bodies the ministry dispatches - which exercises water administration in the Huai River basin across Anhui, Henan, Jiangsu and Shandong, and is based in Bengbu, Anhui. It runs the basin's flood forecasting system and can control releases into polder areas during floods.

Hubei Provincial Transport Department.desc: The department of the Hubei provincial government responsible for the province's road network and its inland waterways; it was formerly called the Hubei Provincial Communications Department (HPCD). It manages Hubei's road sector and was the executing agency for four earlier World Bank transport loans in the province.

sources.title: China - Hubei Shiman Highway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P081749)
China - Fifth Inland Waterways Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P085333)

It manages Hubei's road sector and was the executing agency for four earlier World Bank transport loans in the province.

Kunming Railway Bureau.desc: One of the 18 regional railway bureaus of China's state railway system - administrations, attached to the former Ministry of Railways and from 2013 to China Railway Corporation, that operate and maintain the network in their area; the Kunming bureau's area includes Yunnan province. All 18 bureaus were re-registered in November 2017 as companies wholly owned by China Railway Corporation.

Liaoning Urban Construction and Renewal.desc: A project office set up under the Liaoning Provincial Construction Department, in north-east China, to run the day-to-day work of this World Bank loan at provincial level, with a project management office in each of the six project cities. The Bank's completion report records no activity for it outside the loan.

sources.title: China - Liaoning Medium Cities Infrastructure Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P099992)

Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Develo.desc: A ministry of the Vietnamese government, responsible for state management of agriculture, forestry, salt production, aquaculture, irrigation, disaster prevention and rural development. It was merged with the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment to form the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, which began work on 1 March 2025.

sources.title: Decree No. 105/2022/ND-CP defining the functions, tasks, powers and organizational structure of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, Article 1
New Ministry of Agriculture and Environment established to boost efficiency

Ministry of Industry and Trade of Vietna.desc: A ministry of the Vietnamese government, responsible for state management of industry and trade. Its remit covers electricity, new and renewable energy, oil and gas, machinery, metals, chemicals, mining, consumer and food manufacturing, domestic distribution, imports and exports, competition and consumer protection. It replaced the former Ministry of Industry.

sources.title: Decree No. 189/2007/ND-CP defining the functions, tasks, powers and organizational structure of the Ministry of Industry and Trade, Article 1
Vietnam - Second Rural Energy Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P074688)

Ministry of Railways, Foreign Capital an.desc: The unit of China's Ministry of Railways that managed relations with foreign lenders to railway investment projects, and handled procurement on Bank-financed railway loans. The Ministry of Railways was abolished in 2013 and its operating and construction business passed to China Railway Corporation.

sources.title: China - Third National Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P086515)
China - NanGuang Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P112359)
China Railway Corp becomes China State Railway Group Co

Nanning-Guangzhou Railway Company Limite.desc: A single-purpose Chinese railway company, incorporated in July 2009, which succeeded the NanGuang Railway Company Preparation Group (formed September 2008) to build and then run the Nanning-Guangzhou line.

sources.title: China - NanGuang Railway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P112359)

National Highways Authority of India / M.desc: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is the Government of India's ministry for road transport and the national highway network. In this project it was the sole implementing agency named by the World Bank, and its part of the network was the stretches outside the National Highways Development Programme. The National Highways Authority of India is a separate body: a body corporate with perpetual succession, constituted by the central government under the National Highways Authority of India Act 1988, whose function under section 16 is to develop, maintain and manage the national highways; its members are appointed by the central government, which may direct it on questions of policy.

sources.title: India - National Highways Interconnectivity Improvement Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P121185)
Projects API record for P121185, National Highways Interconnectivity Improvement Project (implementing agency field)

National Highways Authority of India / M.note: Compound key naming two bodies. The Bank's completion report and its project record name only the Ministry as the implementing agency for this project, and present the Authority as the implementing agency of a different programme; see the discrepancies entry.

Northern, Central, Southern, Hanoi and H.desc: The five electricity distribution subsidiaries of Vietnam Electricity (EVN): the Hanoi, Northern, Central, Southern and Ho Chi Minh City Power Corporations. Each distributes and retails electricity at 220 kV, 110 kV and below in its own franchise area, through subsidiary power companies that own the medium- and low-voltage networks, and buys directly from power plants of 30 MW or less. As of 2011 about 75 per cent of the distribution networks supplying rural households were theirs.

sources.title: Vietnam - Distribution Efficiency Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P125996)

Northern, Central, Southern, Hanoi and H.note: Compound key naming five bodies; see the discrepancies entry.

SMEC.desc: An Australian engineering consultancy working on transport, energy, water and built-environment infrastructure, from feasibility study and design through to construction supervision and commissioning. It traces its origin to 1949 and the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Scheme in New South Wales. In 2016 it had about 5,800 employees and more than 75 offices; on 1 August 2016 Surbana Jurong of Singapore announced it would buy 100 per cent of the firm for about S$400 million, and SMEC now describes itself as a member of the Singapore-headquartered Surbana Jurong Group.

sources.title: Surbana Jurong acquires SMEC to be one of Asia's largest consultancy powerhouses in urban and infrastructure developments
About us

SMEC.note: The case events are of 2010, before the Surbana Jurong purchase. The 16,000-plus employee figure on SMEC's current site is not used here because the page does not say whether it is SMEC's or the group's.

Shaanxi Provincial Communications Depart.desc: The department of the Shaanxi provincial government, in north-west China, responsible for the provincial and national roads in the province, including the province's expressways and the allocation of maintenance resources for those roads.

sources.title: China - Shaanxi Ankang Road Development Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P075613)

Shaanxi Provincial Communications Depart.note: The name is as the World Bank's completion report gives it. Counterpart departments in Hubei, Guangdong and Guangxi were renamed from 'Communications Department' to 'Transport Department' in the same period; see the discrepancies entry.

Shiyan Municipal Government.desc: The city government of Shiyan, a city in north-western Hubei, China, which the World Bank's completion report describes at appraisal in 2004 as an industrial centre with a strong automobile industry, mineral resources and tourism, and a population of over 3 million. A Shiyan City Communications Bureau handles its road work.

sources.title: China - Hubei Shiman Highway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P081749)

Tongyuan Road Construction Development C.desc: A state-owned road construction company in Guiyang, Guizhou, China. Until 2010 it was held by the Guiyang State Assets Management Commission; its holding was then transferred to the newly created state-owned Guiyang Transport and Development Investment Group.

sources.title: China - Guiyang Transport Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P093963)
